originalTitle: Senate committee delays vote on Todd Blanche attorney general nomination – US politics live
summary: Spokesperson says ‘work continues to secure sufficient support’ for Trump pick amid concern over IRS settlement
content: The Senate judiciary committee has postponed a vote, scheduled for Thursday, on the nomination of Todd Blanche, Donald Trump’s former criminal defense lawyer, to be attorney general. Blanche, who holds the role on an acting basis, apparently lacks the votes of two Republican senators who want him to confirm in writing that the Department of Justice will not proceed with a $1.776bn fund to compensate Trump supporters who stormed the Capitol on January 6 2021, or a pledge to forever bar the IRS from investigating the tax returns of the president and his family. The two senators, Thom Tillis of North Carolina and John Cornyn of Texas, both lost their re-election bids this year in Republican primaries in which Trump backed their opponents. A spokesperson for the committee, which is chaired by Iowa Republican Chuck Grassley said in a statement: “Chairman Grassley works to set President Trump’s nominees up for success in committee, not failure. Senators Cornyn and Tillis want written assurances from the Department of Justice regarding the Trump-IRS settlement. Tomorrow’s markup is postponed as work continues to secure sufficient support in committee to favorably report Attorney General-nominee Todd Blanche, who is highly qualified for the job.” In a new ad released on Wednesday, Barack Obama, the former president who installed basketball hoop on the White House tennis court, endorsed the US Senate campaign of Iowa Democrat Josh Turek, a state lawmaker who played wheelchair basketball in four Paralympic Games, winning two gold medals. The ad shows the two men talking about Obama’s win in the 2008 Iowa caucuses, and Turek’s hope to flip a Republican-held Senate seat in the upcoming midterms as they shoot hoops, playing a modified game of Horse called I-O-W-A. Obama’s temporary conversion of the White House tennis court into a place to shoot hoops was recently mocked by his successor, Donald Trump, in an appearance on a podcast to encourage children to read, Storytime with the Second Lady. In the podcast episode, released over the Fourth of July weekend, Trump read, and commented on, an illustreated children’s book called President’s Play, about the sporting activities of presidents through the years. When he came to a part of the book that showed Jimmy Carter playing on the White House tennis court, and the text on the next page read, “President Barack Obama used the same court for basketball”, Trump said instead: “Barack Hussein Obama, he used the same court for basketball”. “There’s a picture of each,” he added. “Jimmy as a tennis player. Barack Hussein Obama as a basketball player. I don’t know if he’s a good basketball player. I tend to doubt it. Actually, his favorite sport is golf.” When the second lady, Usha Vance, replied, “Oh, is that right?” Trump added another gratuitous dig, with a perhaps racist undertone: “Yeah. But he won’t be in the Masters anytime soon.” Trump, who mentioned Obama’s Arabic middle name an average of once a year during his first three years as president, has seemed obsessed with pronouncing the name at every opportunity during his second term, almost treating it like an insulting nickname. A review of speech transcripts and remarks reveals that, in the past six months, Trump has referred to Obama by his full name 60 times, including in those comments addressed at children. On multiple occasions, Trump has credited Rush Limbaugh, the influential far-right radio host he gave a Presidential Medal of Freedom to before his death, with coming up with the idea to use Obama’s middle name as a kind of slur. The US Senate on Wednesday unanimously passed a resolution declaring its opposition to any presidential pardon for Ghislaine Maxwell, the longtime Jeffrey Epstein associate who is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence for sex-trafficking crimes. Introduced by Senator Jacky Rosen, a Democrat of Nevada, the resolution states that Maxwell “should not be granted a Presidential pardon or any form of clemency for her crimes with Jeffrey Epstein relating to the sexual exploitation and abuse of minors”. Although Senate resolutions like these are non-binding and symbolic, Rosen’s office noted in a news release in February when she introduced the measure that the resolution was “designed to put the Senate on record opposing the prospect” of Donald Trump of granting a pardon or clemency to Maxwell. “It’s frankly horrifying that Trump would entertain the idea of clemency for even a second for a convicted sex trafficker,” Rosen said in a floor speech on Wednesday. The resolution was brought on Wednesday, as the Senate weighed Trump’s nomination of Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, to stay in the role permanently. Rosen said its unanimous passage sent a clear message to the White House and Blanche that “there should be NO special treatment for Ghislaine Maxwell”. Marjorie Taylor Greene, the former Maga congresswoman, announced on Wednesday that she was married on Tuesday in Las Vegas to another recent exile from Donald Trump’s good graces, Brian Glenn, the self-described “Maga mouthpiece” who quit his job as White House correspondent for the far-right network Real America’s Voice after his fiancee was cast out by the president for supporting the release of the Epstein files and criticizing his bombing of Iran in 2025. Glenn, who announced his resignation on the air in May, had previously been an openly partisan supporter of Trump, even on the job, mixing praise for the president into his questions for him, which were often phrased to help Trump push his talking points. Before Trump’s rift with Greene, he had eagerly called on Glenn at Oval Office events, using him as a lifeline to avoid potentially awkward or challenging questions from non-partisan reporters. chineseSummary: 发言人表示，由于对国税局和解的担忧，“工作仍在继续，为特朗普的人选争取足够的支持”
